# `silk/crypto/md5_sha1`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Compute the 36-byte MD5-SHA1 digest that TLS 1.0 and 1.1 use: MD5 followed by SHA-1.

## When to use
Use [`Md5Sha1`](#Md5Sha1) only where a legacy format names it, such as Node's `md5-sha1` hash or the
TLS 1.0 and 1.1 RSA signatures. Use SHA-256 elsewhere.

## Details
The digest is the 16-byte MD5 digest of the message followed by its 20-byte SHA-1 digest. The
streaming state does not allocate. Call `make`, `update`, and `finish`, or use `hash`.

## Gotchas
MD5 and SHA-1 both permit deliberate collisions, so the pair does not protect data against
tampering. The hash has no object identifier, so [`Digest.objectIdentifier`](./crypto-digest.md#Digest.objectIdentifier) returns an empty
slice.

## Examples
### Hash a message
```silk
import silk.crypto.md5_sha1 { Md5Sha1 }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let digest = Md5Sha1.hash(b"abc")
  // MD5("abc") starts with 90 and SHA-1("abc") with a9.
  if digest[0] != 0x90 || digest[16] != 0xa9 || digest[35] != 0x9d {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Md5Sha1` with `import silk.crypto.md5_sha1 { Md5Sha1 }`.
